ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state organophosphorus/carbonyl structure, with a phosphorus center P on the left, P=O above, two EtO groups connected on the left side, and P also connected to the middle carbon. The middle carbon has one H and is connected to the carbonyl carbon on the right side; the carbonyl carbon on the right side has C=O above and OEt connected on the right side. The figure also has curved arrows and a negatively charged hydrogen, but the question requires ignoring the arrows and excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning count: Counting according to non-hydrogen heavy-atom bonds, the core part includes 1 P=O, 2 P-O bonds, 1 P-C bond, 1 middle C-carbonyl C bond, 1 carbonyl C=O bond, and 1 carbonyl C-OEt bond, for a core total of 7. There are three ethyl Et groups in the structure, and each ethyl contributes two non-hydrogen bonds, O-C and C-C, so 3 × 2 = 6. The total is 7 + 6 = 13.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure, then count heavy-atom bonds by fragments. Count the core non-H connections: P=O = 1, two P-O bonds to EtO groups = 2, P-C to the central carbon = 1, central C-carbonyl C = 1, carbonyl C=O = 1, and carbonyl C-OEt = 1, giving 7 core bonds. Then expand the three ethyl groups: each ethyl contributes O-C and C-C = 2 non-H bonds, so 3 × 2 = 6. Add 7 + 6 to obtain 13.

method.method_draft: Convert the drawing to a heavy-atom connectivity graph. Assign non-H connection counts: P has 4 connections; phosphoryl O has 1; the two P-bound ethoxy O atoms have 2 each; the central carbon has 2 non-H connections; the carbonyl carbon has 3; carbonyl O has 1; the ester O has 2; the three ethyl CH2 carbons have 2 each; the three ethyl CH3 carbons have 1 each.
